'''Team Vitality''' is a French esports organization.

== History ==
'''Team Vitality''' formed its League of Legends team in December 2015 as its first expansion into PC gaming, acquiring [[Gambit Gaming]]'s [[League Championship Series/Europe/2016 Season/Spring Season|EU LCS Spring 2016]] seed. Their first player signed at the time of announcement was former [[H2k]] support [[kaSing]].<ref name="formation">[http://www.team-vitality.fr/news/vitality-acquiert-un-spot-lcs?page=0,1#vitality_acquires_lcs_spot Vitality acquiert un spot LCS] ''team-vitality.fr''</ref> 5 days later, Vitality completed their roster with former Gambit toplaner [[Cabochard]], former [[Copenhagen Wolves|CW]] jungler [[Shook]], former [[Team ROCCAT|ROCCAT]] midlaner [[Nukeduck]] and kaSing's former teammate [[Hjarnan]]. For their coaching staff, Vitality signed former Gambit coach [[Shaunz]].<ref name="fullroster">[http://www.team-vitality.fr/news/decouvrez-notre-roster-league-legends?page=0%2C1#meet-our-league-of-legends-roster Découvrez notre roster League of Legends] ''team-vitality.fr''</ref>

===2016 Season===
====Spring Split EU LCS====
Vitality's roster was considered one of the top lineups in the LCS, and they finished the split in third place at 13-5, behind the surprise first-place [[G2 Esports]] and second-place [[H2k]]. Cabochard and kaSing were elected to the split's All Pro Team, as the most outstanding players in their positions. In the [[League Championship Series/Europe/2016 Season/Spring Playoffs|playoffs]], however, they were upset by the sixth-place [[Fnatic]] and eliminated in the quarterfinals.

====Summer Split EU LCS====
Before the start of the split, jungler [[Shook]] and AD carry [[Hjarnan]] departed the team, the latter due to health reasons. Vitality signed [[Mightybear]], the former jungler of the LSPL team [[Newbee]], and AD carry [[Police (Park Hyeong-gi)|Police]] of NA LCS [[Apex Gaming]] and formerly [[ESC Ever]].<ref>[http://www.gosugamers.net/lol/news/35563-team-vitality-acquires-mightybear-and-police Team Vitality acquires Mightybear and Police] ''gosugamers.net''</ref>

In the summer split, Vitality failed to live up to prior standards, accruing only three match wins throughout the season with a 3-9-6 series record. Shook returned after four weeks of play and became the starting jungler once again.<ref>[http://www.riftherald.com/2016/6/29/12058736/team-vitality-roster-lineup-mightybear-shook Vitality benches Mightybear, names Shook starting jungler] ''riftherald.com''</ref> After a tiebreaker against [[FC Schalke 04]], Vitality solidified seventh place and avoided playing in relegation series, although they also missed the playoffs.

===2017 Season===
Prior to the start of the competitive season, Vitality again overhauled its roster. First, Vitality hired on [[Steeelback]], the AD carry of [[Team ROCCAT]], to replace the departing Police.<ref>[https://dotesports.com/league-of-legends/steeelback-vitality-2017-3867 Steeelback joins Team Vitality for 2017 season] ''dotesports.com''</ref> Next, the team picked up [[Hachani]], the former support player of top-tier LCK team [[KT Rolster]], to replace kaSing.<ref>[http://www.espn.com/esports/story/_/id/18183335/2016-league-legends-team-vitality-drops-kasing-tries-hachani Team Vitality drops KaSing, tries out Hachani] ''espn.com''</ref> In the jungle, Vitality initially looked toward [[Afreeca Freecs]] jungler [[LirA]],<ref>[http://www.espn.com/esports/story/_/id/18188957/league-legends-team-vitality-signs-lira-offseason-roster-shuffle-sources-say Updated: Former Afreeca jungler LirA to join Team Vitality] ''espn.com''</ref> but the deal unexpectedly fell through, as LirA felt uncomfortable with the change. Vitality instead wound up signing [[GBM]], formerly of the NA LCS's [[NRG eSports]], as well as [[Djoko]] of the EU CS team [[Millenium]].<ref>[http://www.espn.com/esports/story/_/id/18311461/league-legends-roster-shuffle-gbm-signed-jungler-team-vitality Confirmed: GBM signed as jungler for Team Vitality] ''espn.com''</ref><ref>[http://wwg.com/esports/2017/01/06/team-vitality-announce-roster-djoko-to-start/ Team Vitality Announce Roster, Djoko to Start] ''wwg.com''</ref> Djoko earned the starting jungler spot while GBM became a substitute; [[Alderiate]] and [[AoD]] also signed with the team as substitutes. 

====Spring Split ====
With the reorganization of the EU LCS regular season format, Vitality was drafted into [[EU LCS/2017_Season/Spring_Season|Group B]] along with [[Origen]], [[H2k Gaming]], [[Splyce]], and [[Unicorns of Love]]. After opening the season with a paltry 1-3 record over three weeks, support player [[Hachani]] was benched.<ref name="hachanibenched">[http://www.team-vitality.fr/news/changes-our-league-legends-roster Changes to our League of Legends roster] ''team-vitality.fr''</ref> Three days later, [[GBM]] moved to the starting mid laner position, while [[Nukeduck]] took over the empty support role. Because continuous lack of success they kept shuffeling their roster around without significant improvement and ended far out of reach of playoff positions in 4th place of the group only beating Origen twice and last place of Group A [[Giants Gaming]].

==== Summer Split ====
For [[EU LCS/2017_Season/Summer_Season|Summer Split]] Vitality signed support [[VandeR]] and got picked into a nearly identical Group B with promoted [[Mysterious Monkeys]] instead of Origen. The roster change helped them improved their performance a  bit but they still only managed to place 4th in their group missing out on playoffs again and ending their season early.

=== 2018 Season ===
==== Spring Split ====
Team Vitality rebuilt their new roster around toplaner Cabochard going into Season 8 and signed [[Gilius]] along rookies [[Jiizuké]], [[Minitroupax]], and [[Jactroll]] who had won the Spring Promotion with Giants. They had an excellent 7-1 start to the [[EU LCS/2018_Season/Spring_Season|Spring Split]] with their explosive and entertaining playstyle but as the other teams figured out how to slow them down they dropped down and finished the Regular Season in 4th place with a 10-8 record. They ended up in 4th place after playoffs as well after beating [[H2k Gaming]] 3-2 in quarterfinals and losing to Fnatic 1-3 semifinals and third-place match against Splyce 2-3 in close series.

==== Summer Split ====
Following a mediocre start to [[EU LCS/2018_Season/Summer_Season|Summer Split]] they signed [[Kikis]] after week 5 with a 5-5 record hoping that he could improve the roster. Because this roster change worked out and Vitality finished the Regular Season in 2nd place after winning tiebreaker games against [[FC Schalke 04]] and [[G2 Esports]] Gilius decided to step away from the team as they were performing better with Kikis. In semifinals they lost against a strong Schalke team but by beating [[Misfits (European Team)|Misfits]] 3-1 in third-place match they had earned the second most [[EU LCS/2018 Season/Championship Points|championship points]] to qualify for the [[2018 Season World Championship|World Championship]] as Europe's 2nd seed.

==== 2018 World Championship ==== 
At the [[2018 Season World Championship/Main Event|World Championship]] they were drawn into group B with LCK third seed [[Gen.G]], NA LCS third seed [[Cloud 9]] and LPL favorite [[Royal Never Give Up]]. After going 1-2 in week 1 they upset RNG in week 2 and ended the group with a 3-3 record which meant they exited Worlds early but earned lots of respect for showing the western regions that chinese and korean teams are not unbeatable. This wasn't really satisfying though as they unnecessarily lost both games against Cloud 9 while in the end one win would have been enough to reach quarterfinals.

=== 2019 Season ===
On November 20, Riot Games announced Team Vitality as one of the ten partner teams for the [[LEC/2019 Season/Spring Season|LEC 2019 Spring Split]].<ref>[https://eu.lolesports.com/en/articles/league-of-legends-european-championship-is-here Take a closer look at the LEC] ''eu.lolesports.com''</ref>

==== Spring Split ====
For Season 9 Vitality signed promising jungler [[Mowgli]] from LCK team [[Afreeca Freecs]] and started off the Split strong yet again looking like a top 3 team before dropping off a bit and finished the Regular Season in 5th place at 10-8. In the quarterfinal series against Fnatic who got to choose which team they wanted to face they had some early leads but just as their opponents predicted they did not manage to snowball these and lost the series 0-3.

==== Summer Split ====
Vitality had a bad start in [[LEC/2019 Season/Summer Season|Summer Split]]. They lost all 4 games in the first two weeks getting heavily criticized by viewers before especially Attila turned up and carried the team for a few weeks. This did not hold on though and after losing their last 6 games of regular season they faced SK who were on an upswing in a tiebreaker for 6th place and therefore playoff participation. Going onto comfort picks they managed to beat SK and faced Schalke in Round 1 of playoffs. After game 1 went completely wrong from level 1 onwards they recovered for game 2 but ultimately lost the bloody series 1-3 and therefore their season ended early as they did not accumulate enough championship points to qualify for Regional Finals.

=== 2020 Season ===
Following this they had to find a replacement for Jiizuke who chose to go to NA. They also decided to sign [[Duke (Hadrien Forestier) | Duke]] from Splyce as new headcoach and picked up rookies [[Milica]] and [[Comp]] from ERL teams [[Vodafone Giants.Spain | Vodafone Giants]] and [[Team LDLC]] and [[Skeanz]] from their own academy team. Following this Attila left the organisation. Due to VISA issues for Milica to join the team in germany they decided to split scrim time with academy mid lander Saken once again which had a negative impact on their performance at the start of [[LEC/2020 Season/Spring Season|Spring Split]] where they started off 0-6. With playoffs starting to getting out of reach they first started to switch the roster up by promoting Steeelback from the academy team. As this did not bring the needed improvements and Milica being unable to travel due to the [[2019–20 Coronavirus Pandemic]] they decided to sign [[Selfie]] for the reminder of the split for Saken to continue developing in academy and managed to pick up a comeback victory against Fnatic on the last day which still saw them in 10th place with a 2-16 record.

== Trivia ==
* Vitality's 7-11 finish in [[LEC/2019 Season/Summer Season|LEC 2019 Summer]] is tied (with [[Rogue (European Team)|Rogue]] in the same split) for the fewest games won by a playoff team in an 18 game season.
